policies.title: Corporal Punishment
candidates: Corporal punishment is a possible consequence only for certain types of student misconduct.

Each school's student behavior management plan (see Board policy 4302, School Plan for Management of Student Behavior) shall specify the types of student misconduct that may result in corporal punishment.
Corporal punishment shall be administered in accordance with G.S.
The student body shall be informed beforehand what general types of misconduct could result in corporal punishment.

Unless the acts of misconduct are overt, extreme and disruptive, corporal punishment should not be used unless other lesser punishments have been tried first and unless the student has been warned that corporal punishment may be the result of further misbehavior.
This board policy regarding corporal punishment shall be available to all students and their parents or guardians at the beginning of the school year.
Minimal procedural due process shall be accorded the student in cases where corporal punishment is administered.
Corporal punishment shall not be administered in a classroom where other students are present.
Only a principal, assistant principal, or teacher may administer corporal punishment and may only do so in the presence of a principal, assistant principal, or teacher.
Prior to corporal punishment being administered, the witness and student must be told beforehand and in each other's presence the reason for the punishment.
The age, sex, size and general physical and mental health of the student shall be considered before corporal punishment is administered.
Corporal punishment must not be administered in anger.
In no event may excessive force be used in the administration of corporal punishment.
Corporal punishment shall not be administered on a student whose parent has stated in writing that corporal punishment may not be administered on that student.

The form will advise the parent that the student may be subject to suspension, among other possible consequences, for offenses that would otherwise not result in suspension if corporal punishment were administered instead.
If the parent does not return the form, corporal punishment may be administered on the student.
The principal or designee shall provide the student's parent or guardian with notification that corporal punishment has been administered.

The person who administered the corporal punishment shall provide the student's parent or guardian a written explanation of the reason for the administration of corporal punishment and the name of the witness who was present.

A record of each administration of corporal punishment shall be kept by the principal and shall include the date and time of administration, the names of the individuals present and the reason for the administration of the punishment.

115C-390.4(c) the board will report to the State Board of Education, in a manner prescribed by the State Board of Education, on the number of times that corporal punishment has been administered during the year.
The number of students who received corporal punishment.

The number of students who received corporal punishment who were also students with disabilities and were eligible to receive special education and related services under the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Improvement Act, 20 U.S.C.
The grade level of the students who received corporal punishment.
The race, gender and ethnicity of the students who received corporal punishment.
The reason for the administration of the corporal punishment for each student who received corporal punishment.

policies.title: Corporal Punishment - Students with Disabilities
candidates: 115C-391, corporal punishment may not be used on a student with a disability as defined by G.S.

115C-106.3(1) or on a student with a disability who is covered under Section 504 of the federal Rehabilitation Act of 1973 if the student's parent or guardian has stated in writing that corporal punishment must not be administered on that student.

If the parent has not returned the form stating in writing that corporal punishment must not be used on the student, then the parent or guardian must be presented with the form at the first individualized education program or Section 504 meeting held during the school year.

policies.title: School Plan for Management of Student Behavior
candidates: (See policy 4341, Parental Involvement in Student Behavior Issues.) No school plan for managing student behavior may authorize the use of corporal punishment.
Corporal punishment is the intentional infliction of physical pain upon the body of a student as a disciplinary measure.
It includes, but is not limited to, spanking, paddling and slapping.
The board prohibits corporal punishment, believing that other consequences are more appropriate and effective for teaching self-control.
No teacher, substitute teacher, student teacher, bus driver, or other employee, contractor or volunteer may use corporal punishment to discipline any student.
Reasonable force that is necessary to protect oneself or others is not considered corporal punishment.
